content:
Update your real estate headshot every two years, and immediately when you change brokerage, change your look, or the photo no longer matches the person who arrives at the door. Two years is the ceiling, not the target. Most agents hit one of the triggers below well before the calendar does.

Agents cannot get away with the five-year-old photo that other professions quietly keep. Your face is on the sign at the end of the drive, on the mailer through the letterbox and on the brokerage page, so the neighbourhood sees it far more often than any LinkedIn contact would.

How often should a real estate agent update their headshot?

Every two years as a default, and sooner the moment something changes. A new brokerage, a new market segment, a new haircut, a beard, glasses, or a noticeable change in weight all count.

The simplest test needs no calendar: stand next to your own yard sign. If a buyer would need a second look to confirm you are the same person, the photo is already overdue.

That test matters because, according to the National Association of REALTORS, 88 percent of buyers and 91 percent of sellers used an agent in 2025. The photo is often the first thing those people see of you.

Why do real estate headshots date faster than other professions?

Because the photo is physical and local. A consultant's headshot lives on a profile that people glance at once. An agent's headshot is printed on signs, bus benches, mailers and listing flyers that the same few thousand households see week after week.

Repetition makes drift obvious. A neighbour who has walked past your sign for three years knows exactly what the photo looks like, and they also know what you look like now. Any gap between the two gets noticed, and it gets noticed by the people most likely to refer you.

What does a mismatched photo cost you?

Trust, and it costs it fast. LinkedIn's own photo guidelines require a profile photo to reflect your likeness, and that principle applies to every place your face appears, not just one platform. The person who arrives should be the person on the sign.

The judgment happens before you say hello. Princeton researchers found that people form impressions of trustworthiness and competence after about 100 milliseconds of seeing a face, and longer looks mostly increase confidence rather than change the verdict.

A seller who has already formed an impression from a ten-year-old sign then has to reconcile it with you at the door. That small moment of recalibration is not where you want a listing appointment to start.

Which triggers mean you should refresh now?

Do not wait for the two-year mark if any of these apply. Tick the ones that are true today.

  • You moved to a new brokerage, or your brokerage rebranded its colours or sign design.
  • You moved into a new market segment, for example from starter homes to luxury or from residential to commercial.
  • Your hair, beard, glasses or weight have changed enough that a stranger would pause.
  • The photo is more than two years old, regardless of how it looks.
  • Your signage, mailers and website currently show two or more different photos of you.
  • A client has ever said "you look different from your picture".

One tick is enough. Two or more means the refresh is overdue and is probably already costing you referrals you will never hear about.

Why did agents put off refreshing, and why is that over?

Refreshing used to be a budget decision. A studio session meant booking weeks ahead, a morning away from showings, and a bill that made a lot of agents decide the old photo was fine for another year. That is how a two-year rule quietly becomes a six-year reality.

That trade-off has gone. With real estate agent headshots from Picturesk you upload 5 to 15 recent selfies, choose your backgrounds and outfits, and we train a model on your face and email a full-resolution set in about an hour. Sets are $9, $29 or $49, paid once, with no subscription.

If the results do not look like you, tell us within 3 days of delivery and you get a full refund.

At that price and speed, a refresh every two years stops being a project and becomes a Tuesday-afternoon task. It also means you can refresh the day you switch brokerage rather than months later.

How do you refresh without breaking your brand?

Keep the background the same and change only the person. Your signage and mailers work partly on recognition, so a new photo that keeps the same setting reads as an update, while a completely different style reads as a different agent.

The Picturesk catalogue names its backgrounds, which makes this easy to repeat. If your last set used In-office, choose In-office again.

Warm neutral and Bright and natural suit agents who want an approachable look, while Corporate studio suits luxury and commercial work. Pair it with the same outfit family as before, whether that is Business casual (collared shirt), Blazer over tee or Business suit.

Then replace every copy at once: the sign template, the mailer, the brokerage page, your AI headshot generator set for social profiles, and your email signature. Two photos in circulation is the exact problem you are trying to fix.

faqs.question: How old is too old for a real estate agent headshot?
faqs.answer: Two years is the ceiling for agents, and accuracy matters more than age. A photo that still matches the person who turns up at the door is fine at eighteen months, while a one-year-old photo from before a beard, new glasses or a brokerage change is already overdue. If a client has ever said you look different in person, replace it now.

faqs.question: Should I get a new headshot when I change brokerage?
faqs.answer: Yes, and do it before the new signs are printed. A brokerage change is the cleanest moment to refresh because every template is being rebuilt anyway, and a new photo in the new brand colours reads as one deliberate move. Reusing the old photo means your face carries the old brokerage into the new one.

faqs.question: Should my headshot be the same on my sign, mailers and website?
faqs.answer: Yes, one current photo everywhere. Signs and mailers work on recognition, so two different photos in circulation splits that recognition and makes people wonder which one is you. When you refresh, replace every copy at once: sign template, mailers, brokerage page, social profiles and email signature.
